refuted.fact: verified_facts[15]: "The signatory list printed in the version fetched on 2026-09-16 contains 235 bulleted names."
refuted.why: 235 is correct for that PDF (I recounted: 235 entries, 234 bullet separators) but it is a STALE snapshot and must not be used as the letter's signatory count. The identical letter is hosted first-party by another signatory at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/topics/open-weight/ (HTTP 200, datePublished 2026-07-24T09:48:44+00:00, dateModified 2026-08-11T00:22:42+00:00), same title, same July 24 2026 date, same body text. That copy lists 273 organizations - a strict superset of NVIDIA's 235, with 38 extra entries (Docker, Dropbox, Asana, Spotify, Snyk, SambaNova, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, ...) and ZERO entries present in NVIDIA's copy but absent from Microsoft's - and states in its own words: "More than 270 companies and organizations have signed the 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership' open letter as of August 3, 2026." NVIDIA's PDF carries no as-of date at all. Two further wording problems in the same fact: the PDF contains ZERO occurrences of "signator"/"signatories" and never labels or captions the list, so "the signatory list" is the researcher's label, not the document's; and the entries are organization names, not personal "names". Note that wordpress.org/news/2026/08/open-weight/ (first-party, HTTP 200) links the Microsoft page - not the NVIDIA PDF - as the letter.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[2]: "The same sentence is the page's meta description."
refuted.why: It is not. The meta description (and og:description) is two sentences: "NVIDIA has agreed to acquire Hugging Face. Together, we will scale Hugging Face's platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide." The quoted sentence is only its second half.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[7] verbatim_quote: "NVIDIA has released more than 500 models on Hugging Face and more than 250 open datasets. ... NVIDIA is the largest contributor of open models and data to Hugging Face, and our contributions continue to grow."
refuted.why: The two sentences are in the OPPOSITE order in the source. The body reads "NVIDIA is the largest contributor of open models and data to Hugging Face, and our contributions continue to grow." and THEN, as the next paragraph, "NVIDIA has released more than 500 models on Hugging Face and more than 250 open datasets." An ellipsis-joined verbatim_quote that reverses source order is not verbatim, and here it inverts which claim frames which. The researcher's prose summary had the order right; the JSON record - the artifact that will actually be used - has it wrong.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[28]: "the dataset config renderer no longer evaluates template expressions in data fields nor processes HDF5 external references".
refuted.why: The source says "nor WRONGLY processes HDF5 external references" (huggingface.co/blog/agent-intrusion-technical-timeline, "What we changed"). Dropping "wrongly" turns a bug fix into removal of the feature. Hugging Face did not say it stopped processing HDF5 external references.

refuted.fact: verified_facts[28]: "the internal service-connector credential narrowed to one per cluster".
refuted.why: The source says: "the internal service-connector should not have returned a full cluster catalog to a single ephemeral client. This was a subtle configuration flaw in our cluster access system. We patched it, and each cluster is now fully isolated." There is no statement about one credential per cluster. The same fact also silently drops two items the source lists under the same heading: "We switched to workload identity when it was not yet implemented", and under Better detection "tighter enforcement of network origins, plus tooling that flags tokens used from unexpected origins". verified_facts[28] carries no verbatim_quote at all and is the only long unquoted paraphrase in the record.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[14]: "The open letter Huang refers to is 'Open Weights and American AI Leadership'", recorded with is_vendor_claim:false.
unsupported.why: No page I fetched says this. In the NVIDIA post the phrase "Recently, I coauthored an open letter on the importance of open weights to the AI economy" is PLAIN TEXT with no hyperlink - I enumerated every <a> inside the <article> element and the only in-body link is "open model" -> https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/open-models/. The letter itself never names him: "Huang" and "Jensen" both return 0 occurrences across all 5 PDF pages, and the document names no author at all. So both the identification of the letter AND Huang's coauthorship are inferences; neither can carry is_vendor_claim:false. The article may write only that Huang says he coauthored an open letter on open weights, and separately that NVIDIA hosts a letter of that title. The URL itself is NOT a guess - it is returned by search restricted to nvidia.com domains - so rule 6 is not triggered, but the record never says how it was found, which it should.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[14] verbatim_quote: "Open Weights and American AI Leadership / July 24, 2026".
unsupported.why: A composite the researcher assembled with an inserted " / ". The PDF has the title on two lines and the date after a blank line; those characters are not adjacent in the document. It survives a normalised match only because the separator normalises away. A verbatim_quote field must not contain invented punctuation.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[13]: "NVIDIA did not issue a separate newsroom press-release page for the acquisition."
unsupported.why: True as far as I can establish, but it is an inference from a 20-item feed window, not something the feed states, and the record presents it as fact. I corroborated it by a route the researcher did not use - https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news?q=Hugging%20Face (HTTP 200) returns only https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-to-acquire-hugging-face/ plus an unrelated LeRobot blog post, no nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/... release. Record the method, not just the conclusion.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[24]: "between 2026-07-09 02:28 UTC and 2026-07-13 14:14 UTC - about a 4.5-day campaign".
unsupported.why: The window and the phrase "4.5-day campaign" are both in the source, but the same post's TL;DR says "Over roughly two and a half days inside our infrastructure". The 4.5 days is the whole window including Stage 1 on OpenAI's and a third party's infrastructure; only ~2.5 days were inside Hugging Face. Recording only 4.5 days invites the article to say the attacker was inside Hugging Face for 4.5 days, which the source does not say.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[22] and [27] read as if the 2026-07-16 post and the 2026-07-27 post name different models for the forensic work (zai-org/GLM-5.2 vs nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4).
unsupported.why: The 2026-07-27 post names BOTH: its TL;DR says "Using open-weights models, in particular zai-org/GLM-5.2", and its analysis section says "We stood up the quantized version of ZAI's GLM-5.2 by Nvidia ( nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 ) on our own infrastructure". There is no discrepancy between the two posts, and an article must not present one.

unsupported.fact: Record-level: verified_facts 13, 29, 30 and 31 are sourced only to feeds and a search API (nvidianews releases.xml, openai.com/news/rss.xml, efts.sec.gov, huggingface.co/blog/feed.xml), none of which may appear in the article's sources list per the researcher's own must_not_write.
unsupported.why: Not a factual error, but it means four recorded facts will have no traceable URL in the published article. Anything written from them - the 8-K's existence, OpenAI's two post titles, the absence of a Hugging Face announcement - needs either an article-page source or explicit in-text attribution to the official feed.

additional_findings: BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE, MISSED: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001045810.json returns HTTP 200 (159,883 bytes) here. It is SEC's own submissions API and is a cleaner citation than efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index. It confirms every element of verified_facts[30] (accession 0001045810-26-000078, form 8-K, items 8.01, filingDate 2026-09-03, reportDate 2026-09-02, primaryDocument nvda-20260902.htm, fileNumber 000-23985) AND adds a fact the researcher does not have: acceptanceDateTime 2026-09-03T12:03:56.000Z - about 7 minutes AFTER the blog post's article:published_time (11:56:49+00:00) and 4 minutes after the newsroom RSS pubDate (11:59:49 GMT). The blog came first, the 8-K second, both on 2026-09-03. This strengthens the decision to keep the slug at 20260903 and should be recorded.

MATERIAL PARAGRAPH MISSED from the NVIDIA post: "NVIDIA has been committed to open weight models for years, demonstrated by multiyear investments and major contributions to open source platforms, including Hugging Face. NVIDIA has said that open models, data and tools broaden access to AI, and it has contributed hundreds of open models and datasets to Hugging Face as part of that effort." It gives a THIRD figure, "hundreds", alongside the 500+/250+ counts, and it is written in the third person inside an otherwise first-person post - a reason to treat it as corporate boilerplate rather than Huang's voice.

MATERIAL PARAGRAPH MISSED - NVIDIA's policy argument, which is what actually connects the deal to the open-weights framing: "Open models let startups, businesses, universities and public institutions build on advanced capabilities without training every model from scratch. They enable organizations to match the right model to the right job. That is how AI can advance safely, strengthen cybersecurity and sovereignty, accelerate innovation, and reach factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms and Main Street businesses around the world." Followed by the standalone line "AI advances faster when people can build together."

The ONLY hyperlink NVIDIA places in the body of the acquisition post is on the words "open model", pointing to https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/open-models/ (HTTP 200, 437,021 bytes). That is NVIDIA's own definition page and the only definition the post endorses by linking - better anchored than the unlinked PDF for the article's one-clause definition of open weights.

MISSED FIRST-PARTY ATTRIBUTION: the 2026-07-27 technical post's TL;DR states "an autonomous AI agent driven by a combination of OpenAI models ran an end-to-end intrusion against our platform". That is Hugging Face's own on-the-record attribution of whose models drove the attack. The researcher put the question into unverified_or_excluded instead of recording the statement; it belongs in verified_facts with is_vendor_claim:true.

MISSED SELF-REPORTED FAILURE: the same post says its own detection stack "failed to correctly raise the alert's criticality and trigger the on-call team, costing precious time in the response". Omitting it reports only the flattering half of Hugging Face's account.

MISSED EXCULPATIONS OF NAMED THIRD PARTIES, which the article must not garble: "the ExploitGym maintainers and their infrastructure had no involvement in the deployment or operation of that evaluation environment"; the abused harness was "an instance labeled 'CyberGym', deployed by an unknown third party, exposing an arbitrary-code endpoint that upstream CyberGym does not provide"; the third-party sandbox provider is named as Modal and "Modal's infrastructure was not compromised in any way."

MISSED BYLINES: the 2026-07-27 technical post is bylined to four named Hugging Face engineers - Hugo Larcher (hlarcher), Adrien Carreira (XciD), raphael g (raphael-gl), Christophe Rannou (chris-rannou) - whereas the 2026-07-16 disclosure is bylined "system". Published July 27, 2026 and July 16, 2026, both confirmed on-page.

MISSED DETAIL: the two initial-access vectors are named precisely in the technical post - an HDF5 external raw storage dataset read that returned local file contents, and a Jinja2 template injection that executed arbitrary code, both against the same config-driven data loader in production Kubernetes pods. The 2026-07-16 disclosure describes them more loosely as "a remote-code dataset loader and a template-injection in a dataset configuration". Any Chinese rendering should follow the later, precise wording.

MISSED SECOND BREAKDOWN: besides the daily counts (07-09 3,779; 07-10 1,135; 07-11 7,677; 07-12 3,892; 07-13 1,130 - all five verified verbatim), the post carries a phase table: recon 6,191; rce 2,911; dropper 6,972; exfil 56; c2 114; evasion 6; k8s 87; supply-chain 69; tailscale 115. Use one table, not a mix.

The technical post itself cites OpenAI's page as https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/ (with trailing slash) - a first-party Hugging Face page vouching for that URL. I re-tested: HTTP 403 with and without the slash, as is https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-incident-and-the-road-ahead. The researcher's block finding stands.
The open-letter PDF is 5 pages but pages 4 and 5 are BLANK; the letter is 3 pages of content plus the bullet list at the end of page 3. "5 pages" is technically true and practically misleading.

I re-verified the researcher's strongest negative result and it HOLDS, including via a route they did not report: huggingface.co/clem/activity/posts (HTTP 200) shows clem's two most recent HF posts are publishedAt 2025-08-07T16:50:56Z and 2025-06-19T17:46:44Z, with no 2026 post; the 2026-09-03 timestamp visible on that page is an updatedAt on a comment thread under the 2025-08-07 post, not a new post. huggingface.co/api/posts?author=clem returns the SPA shell rather than JSON and huggingface.co/posts/clem is HTTP 401, so those are not usable checks - the activity page is. Zero occurrences of "acquir" on huggingface.co/blog, /blog/community, /clem, /clem/activity/posts or /clem/activity/community. https://huggingface.co/blog/huggingface is HTTP 404.

No source in the record is a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet. On the first-party discipline axis (check 5) the record is clean, and the unverified_or_excluded list correctly quarantines the Yahoo/Bloomberg cash-plus-equity split, the "definitive agreement" headline, the CNBC timing and the discuss.huggingface.co forum sentiment.
